title: A systematic review of the existing parent‐led interventions to promote the psychosocial development of neurodivergent children
abstract: Abstract Background This systematic review takes a transdiagnostic approach to understanding the active components commonly used across evidence‐based interventions, to inform the development of a novel psychosocial intervention for children with Developmental Language Disorder (DLD). Methods Searches were conducted in December 2020, August 2022 and July 2026 of 11 databases, including: PsycINFO, PsycEXTRA, Embase, PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL and MEDLINE. Inclusion criteria was: trials must have compared interventions to a control group, or have an 8‐week follow‐up, include parent‐led components and measures of child psychosocial outcomes, must be published in English after 2000, with participants aged 2–13 years old, who met diagnostic criteria for seven categories of neurodivergence (that share psychosocial difficulties to children with DLD). Synthesis was conducted by coding intervention content using a taxonomy and calculating effect sizes using baseline and follow‐up data on psychosocial outcomes. Quality appraisal was assessed using the National Institute of Health's quality assessment measures. Results A total of 11,583 studies were selected for abstract screening; 52 studies met the pre‐specified inclusion criteria after full‐text screening. All interventions analysed were designed for autistic children ( n = 26) and/or attention deficit hyperactive disorder (ADHD; n = 23). Across studies, 870 children with ADHD and 832 autistic children received interventions; 730 children with ADHD and 701 autistic children received a control. Four intervention components were most used across effective interventions: parent‐child interaction training, parenting behaviours, and emotion management for both parent and child. An association between parent wellbeing and improved child psychosocial outcomes is suggested, however limited by the lack of data. Therapeutic and researcher contact appears to impact intervention engagement. Accessibility is discussed. Conclusion Evidence‐based psychosocial interventions are required for neurodivergent children other than children with autism and ADHD. Psychosocial interventions for children with DLD should consider addressing parent‐child communication, wellbeing of both parent and child, and involve therapeutic support.
